class.name: SuperposSession
class.brief_description: Owner-thread canonical core World access and packed publication.
class.description: Compiled into the EGP engine through its native Superpos module. Full-width unsigned values use signed opaque Variant bits in GDScript and unsigned native metadata in generated C# and C++ bindings.

method.name: acknowledge_packet
method.description: Acknowledges a received message on the selected channel with its checked binding generation. This does not apply application state automatically.

method.name: advance_tick
method.description: Advances the canonical session by one tick on its owning thread. For a world with automatic ticks enabled, manual advancement is rejected.

method.name: attach_receiver
method.description: Equivalent to [method SuperposSpawner.start] for a spawner whose [member SuperposSpawner.session] is this Session. Only one receiver can be attached at a time.

method.name: close
method.description: Closes the session through [method close_checked]. Use the checked method when the caller needs the rejection reason.

method.name: close_checked
method.description: Closes the owned canonical world and transport, subject to owner and lifecycle checks. Retained wrappers cannot revive an owner that has been permanently retired. Called from inside a native callback (for example a [signal simulation_tick] handler or a simulation provider), the close is accepted and returns [constant OK]: [method get_state] reports [code]"Closing"[/code] until the outermost callback returns, and the teardown then runs before control leaves the native call (for example [method advance_tick]). Nothing is torn down while the callback frame is still running. During a managed reload or native retirement custody the close is refused with [constant ERR_BUSY].

method.name: configure
method.description: Creates a bounded canonical world from the supplied schemas, object capacity, authority and state budget. This configures local state; use [method configure_udp] to attach a network association. Calls must run on the owning thread.

method.name: configure_udp
method.description: Attaches one pre-provisioned native UDP server or client association with local/remote endpoints, session ID, peer identity and admission key. Check [method get_admission_state] for authenticated readiness. The admission key is a raw provisioned secret, not a connect token; never log it. The optional [param transport] profile accepts [code]bundle_frames[/code] (default [code]true[/code]: messages, delivery receipts, probes and a piggybacked acknowledgement share each datagram), [code]burst_datagrams[/code] (1-16, default 4 paced datagrams per pump), [code]receive_frames[/code] (1-64, default 64), [code]minimum_rate[/code] (bytes per second, default 0: a real-time budget floor under the congestion window, so random loss on a wireless link cannot starve the stream below it) and [code]channel_modes[/code], an [Array] of up to 32 delivery modes indexed by channel: [code]0[/code] reliable ordered (default), [code]1[/code] reliable unordered, [code]2[/code] unreliable latest (newer messages supersede older ones on the channel) and [code]3[/code] unreliable. [code]channel_purposes[/code] is an [Array] of up to 32 channel purposes: [code]0[/code] application (default) or [code]1[/code] control, a reliable ordered route with a 4 KiB record ceiling and its own reserve. Replication with [SuperposSpawner] and [SuperposReplicationServer] needs channel 0 to be a control channel and channels 1 and 2 to be reliable unordered application channels: [code]channel_modes[/code] 0, 1 and 1 with [code]channel_purposes[/code] 1 for channel 0. Both peers must declare identical channel modes and purposes; admission rejects a mismatch. A client of a single-port server ([SuperposUdpListener]) also passes [code]connection_id[/code], the nonzero connection ID it was admitted with; its datagrams then carry a 9-byte routing prefix, the DTLS payload ceiling shrinks by those 9 bytes so complete datagrams stay within 1,200 bytes, and both ends validate a changed address with an encrypted challenge. [code]connection_id[/code] is rejected for a server; a server uses [method configure_udp_listener]. Unknown keys return [constant ERR_INVALID_PARAMETER]. For example, a client that sends reliable controls on channel 0 and latest-state snapshots on channel 1 passes [code]channel_modes[/code] with the values 0 and then 2 (unreliable latest) and [code]burst_datagrams[/code] 4.

method.name: configure_udp_listener
method.description: Attaches one pre-provisioned server association to a bound single-port [param listener]. [param connection_id] is the nonzero, unpredictable ID admission gave this client; it routes the client's datagrams to this Session and never authenticates. The first handshake datagram binds the client's address, DTLS authenticates the peer with [param admission_key], and a later address change moves outbound traffic only after the client answers an encrypted path challenge. [param session_id], [param peer_identity], [param admission_key] and [param transport] are as in [method configure_udp], except that [code skip-lint]connection_id[/code] is not accepted in [param transport]. Returns [constant ERR_UNCONFIGURED] for an unbound listener and [constant ERR_ALREADY_IN_USE] when another Session already uses [param connection_id]. The Session keeps the listener alive until its network is closed; never log the admission key.

method.name: destroy_object
method.description: Destroys the canonical object identified by the exact handle bits. This does not free an application scene Node.

method.name: detach_receiver
method.description: Drains and detaches the attached native receiver, cancelling pending constructions and retiring projected nodes. Returns [constant OK] when nothing is attached, and [constant ERR_BUSY] from a Session callback or while closing. Prefer [method SuperposSpawner.stop], which also clears the spawner runtime.

method.name: enqueue_packet
method.description: Queues canonical payload bytes on the selected channel. On success the checked Dictionary contains message, connection epoch, binding generation, channel and an Accepted outcome. Acceptance is not an acknowledgement by the receiver.

method.name: get_admission_state
method.description: Returns a checked Dictionary describing transport attachment and authenticated readiness. [code]ready[/code] is false for an unattached or unavailable association; local configuration alone does not authenticate a peer.

method.name: get_last_error
method.description: Returns the last recorded session error. Check each operation return value or its Dictionary [code]error[/code] for that operation outcome.

method.name: get_packet_outcome
method.description: Returns a checked Dictionary describing the tracked message outcome on the selected channel. Stale binding generations and invalid message identities are rejected.

method.name: get_state
method.description: Returns the session lifecycle state. A permanently retired owner cannot be configured again.

method.name: is_network_ready
method.description: Returns [code]true[/code] when the attached transport is admitted with no error and the session is not paused for a managed reload: the [code]ready[/code] field of [method get_admission_state] without building its Dictionary, for per-tick checks across many sessions.

method.name: get_statistics
method.description: Returns a checked Dictionary of canonical world capacity, live objects, tick, binding generation, memory accounting and publication counts. An attached transport adds its counters and readiness; a native UDP/DTLS transport also reports [code]smoothed_rtt_us[/code], [code]retransmit_timeout_us[/code] and [code]retry_ticks[/code], the reliable retransmission interval in pump ticks derived from that timeout and the measured pump cadence. These counters do not establish application scene replication.

method.name: predict_checked
method.description: Runs a checked prediction step for a registered compiled simulation provider using binding generation, authority epoch, tick and input bytes. Script callbacks do not register or qualify native replay capabilities.

method.name: publish_packed
method.description: Validates and applies a bounded packed canonical operation batch atomically. This does not make Godot property setters transactional or implement automatic scene projection.

method.name: read_authority_epoch
method.description: Returns [code]error[/code] and, only on a successful live authority query, [code]value[/code] containing the unsigned authority epoch bits.

method.name: read_binding_generation
method.description: Returns [code]error[/code] and, only on successful owner validation, [code]value[/code] containing the unsigned binding generation bits. Use this value with checked packet and prediction calls.

method.name: read_object
method.description: Returns a checked Dictionary containing the canonical object handle, schema ID, owner, ownership revision, revision, tick and canonical bytes on success. Stale or invalid handles are rejected.

method.name: read_packet
method.description: Reads the next available packet on the selected channel into a checked Dictionary. Success includes payload, message and association metadata. Acknowledge the returned message using its binding generation after application processing.

method.name: read_prediction
method.description: Returns checked prediction bytes and tick for the supplied binding generation and authority epoch. A registered native simulation provider is required.

method.name: read_prediction_info
method.description: Returns checked prediction-history information for the supplied binding generation and authority epoch. Availability does not establish a physics solver integration.

method.name: read_receiver_status
method.description: Returns the attached spawner runtime status, as [method SuperposSpawner.read_status], with [code]attached[/code] set to [code]true[/code]. Without a receiver, returns only [code]error[/code] set to [constant ERR_UNCONFIGURED].

method.name: read_simulation_profile
method.description: Returns the native simulation capability profile. Unregistered sessions do not expose qualified prediction or replay capabilities.

method.name: read_tick
method.description: Returns [code]error[/code] and, only on successful owner/world validation, [code]value[/code] containing the exact unsigned tick bits. Check the error before reading the value.

method.name: reconcile_checked
method.description: Reconciles a registered native prediction history against the supplied canonical bytes, tick and revision. Returns a checked Dictionary; inspect its error before using reconciliation output.

method.name: retire_packet
method.description: Retires the tracked message using the supplied binding generation and channel. Use the checked outcome to decide when the application no longer needs the message.

method.name: spawn_object
method.description: Creates a bounded canonical object using the selected schema, owner and canonical bytes. Returns its unsigned handle bits, or zero on failure. This does not instantiate a scene Node.

method.name: transfer_ownership
method.description: Transfers a canonical object to the supplied owner, checking the expected ownership revision. Use exact unsigned handle, owner and revision bits.

method.name: read_fields
method.description: Reads selected field IDs through the frozen native schema. The result contains error and, only on success, values, revision and binding_generation. Values uses field IDs as keys. Unsigned 64-bit values and IDs preserve signed integer bit patterns; object references remain weak handles. Duplicate or unknown fields fail without returning partial values. No property getters or scripts run.

method.name: publish_fields
method.description: Publishes typed field values keyed by exact field IDs. Checks the expected canonical object revision and every field before publishing a complete replacement. Boolean, integer, floating-point and packed-byte types are checked against the frozen schema. Unsigned values preserve integer bit patterns. Unmentioned fields retain their canonical values. A successful canonical publication does not imply scene projection or remote delivery.

method.name: begin_predicted_spawn
method.description: Allocates a temporary predicted-spawn identity after [method configure_predicted_spawns]. Returns [code]error[/code] and, on success, [code]sequence[/code], [code]epoch[/code] and [code]peer[/code]. Sequences never repeat in an epoch and never alias a World handle; send the sequence to the authority (for example in a typed RPC) and have it echo the sequence in a field of the object it spawns. Returns [constant ERR_OUT_OF_MEMORY] when every row is in use.

method.name: configure_predicted_spawns
method.description: Reserves [param capacity] predicted-spawn rows (1 through 256) on a client Session with a native network association, bound to its authority epoch and local peer. Configure once; a second call returns [constant ERR_ALREADY_IN_USE]. Without a network returns [constant ERR_UNCONFIGURED].

method.name: confirm_predicted_spawn
method.description: Confirms a pending prediction with the authoritative object it became. [param replica] must be a Ready replica received by this Session and owned by the local peer, otherwise [constant ERR_UNAUTHORIZED] (another owner), [constant ERR_BUSY] (still pending) or [constant ERR_INVALID_PARAMETER] (another Session). Confirming the same object again succeeds; confirming one object for two predictions, or a different object for a confirmed one, returns [constant ERR_INVALID_DATA].

method.name: read_field_changes
method.description: Encodes [param values] (keyed by field ID) with the frozen schema against the object's current canonical image without publishing. Returns [code]error[/code] and, on success, [code]changed[/code] (the field IDs whose encoded bytes differ) and [code]revision[/code] (the compared revision). A quantized field changes only when its quantized level changes. Values are type checked exactly as in [method publish_fields].

method.name: read_predicted_spawn
method.description: Returns [code]error[/code] and, for a live row, [code]phase[/code] ([code]pending[/code], [code]confirmed[/code], [code]rejected[/code] or [code]retired[/code]), [code skip-lint]sequence[/code], [code]handle[/code] and [code]ownership_revision[/code]. A confirmed prediction whose replica left this receiver (destroyed, out of interest, ownership reset or rebind) is retired here.

method.name: reject_predicted_spawn
method.description: Marks a pending prediction rejected, for example after the authority refused it. Rejecting again succeeds; a confirmed prediction returns [constant ERR_UNCONFIGURED].

method.name: release_predicted_spawn
method.description: Releases a resolved (confirmed, rejected or retired) prediction row. A pending prediction returns [constant ERR_BUSY]: it must be confirmed or rejected first.
